'''''Scorzoneroides autumnalis''''', commonly called '''autumn hawkbit''',<ref>{{GRIN | ''Scorzoneroides autumnalis'' | 462391 | accessdate = 10 January 2018}}</ref>  is a [[perennial plant]] species, widespread in its native range in Eurasia (from Europe east to western Siberia),<ref>{{cite journal |author=Rosabelle Samuel |author2=Walter Gutermann |author3=Tod F. Stuessy |author4=Claudete F. Ruas |author5=Hans-Walter Lack |author6=Karin Tremetsberger |author7=Salvador Talavera |author8=Barbara Hermanowski |author9=Friedrich Ehrendorfer |name-list-style=amp |year=2006 |title=Molecular phylogenetics reveals ''Leontodon'' (Asteraceae, Lactuceae) to be diphyletic |journal=[[American Journal of Botany]] |volume=93 |issue=8 |pages=1193–1205 |doi=10.3732/ajb.93.8.1193 |pmid=21642184|doi-access=free }}</ref> and introduced in North America.<ref>[http://efloras.org/florataxon.aspx?flora_id=1&taxon_id=250005016 1. ''Leontodon autumnalis'' Linnaeus], ''[[Flora of North America]]'', accessed March 1, 2010</ref>

The plant is sometimes called '''fall dandelion''', because it is very similar to the [[common dandelion]] (one of the main differences being a branched stem with several capitula<ref>[http://www.luontoportti.com/suomi/en/kukkakasvit/autumn-hawkbit Autumn Hawkbit]</ref>), but "yellow fields", covered by this plant appear much later than dandelions, towards the autumn in the Eastern Europe. In the Latin synonym of the plant name, ''Leontodon autumnalis'',<ref name="Parnell">Parnell, J. and Curtis, T, 2012 ''Webb's An Irish Flora''. Cork University Press.{{ISBN|978-185918-4783}}</ref> "leontodon" means "lion's tooth", the same as "dandelion".

==Description==
''Scorzoneroides autumnalis''  is a perennial herb growing to 35 cm high usually with branched stems and several flower-heads each about 30 mm across. The florets are all ligulate and bright yellow. The leaves are all basal and linear-oblong.<ref name="Parnell"/>

==Reproduction==
Flowers in June to October producing [[achenes]].<ref name="Parnell"/>

==Habitat==
Frequent in damp [[grassland]]<ref name="Parnell"/> and meadows.<ref name="Clapham">Clapham, A.R., Tutin, T.G. 1968 Excursion Flora of the British Isles. Cambridge University Press {{ISBN|0-521-04656-4}}</ref>

==Ecology==
The [[fly]] ''[[Tephritis leontodontis]]'' is known to attack the [[Head (botany)|capitula]] of this plant.<ref name="White">{{cite book|author=Ian M. White |year=1988 |title=Tephritid Flies (Diptera: Tephritidea) |pages=1–134 |publisher= [[Royal Entomological Society of London]] | series = [[R.E.S Handbooks|Handbooks for the Identification of British Insects]] |volume=10/5a |isbn=978-0-901546-68-5}}</ref>

==Distribution==
Abundant in [[Ireland]] and [[Great Britain]].<ref name="Clapham"/>
